areas.name: The Island
areas.blurb: The heart of Night City, ringed by water and rebuilt in pieces.

areas.name: Northside
areas.blurb: The land north of the island: megabuildings, the masses, and the military.

areas.name: Mainland
areas.blurb: The overpacked suburbs, struggling to rebuild in the Time of the Red.

areas.name: Southside
areas.blurb: The city's southern sprawl, where Night City frays into the Badlands.

districts.name: Little Europe
districts.blurb: A district divided between classes and times, with old brick buildings standing next to futuristic skyscrapers.

locations.name: Camden Court
locations.blurb: A secure apartment complex favored by Solos and Execs.

locations.name: Chopper’s
locations.blurb: Formerly a butcher’s shop, now a bar. The meat grinder still works if you want to get rid of a body.

locations.name: Continental Brands Vertical Neighborhood
locations.blurb: Housing for Continental Brands employees. A nightmare to navigate due to its “flavors of the world” theming.

locations.name: Cube-A-Rama
locations.blurb: A cube hotel with an original brick exterior.

locations.name: Danger Gal Housing Facility
locations.blurb: Housing for Danger Gal employees. Pink and full of life.

locations.name: Danger Gal Offices
locations.blurb: Home base for Danger Gal, a private investigation and security Neocorp.

locations.name: Fiddler’s Green
locations.blurb: An “Irish” pub that’s about as Irish as green beer on Saint Patty’s day.

locations.name: Greta’s
locations.blurb: The best pool hall in Night City, with a strong lesbian client base.

locations.name: Holy Angels Church
locations.blurb: A Catholic church run by Father Kevin and Father Paul. Known far and wide as neutral ground in Night City.

locations.name: Paradiso Terrestre
locations.blurb: An upscale Southern Neo-Italian dining experience. Meals by appointment only.

locations.name: Short Circuit
locations.blurb: Night City’s premiere Tech and Netrunner bar. Owned and operated by Brain and his husband 3-Piece.

locations.name: Soprano’s
locations.blurb: An Italian restaurant that leans heavily into its mafioso theming. The real mob gives it a pass.

locations.name: Torrell and Chiang’s
locations.blurb: Considered by many to be the best tailors in Night City.

districts.name: Upper Marina
districts.blurb: A bustling district with a mix of old industrial zones and gentrified neighborhoods built around a series of docks and small marinas.

locations.name: The Afterlife
locations.blurb: The premiere edgerunner bar in Night City. Owned by the legendary Solo, Rogue.

locations.name: Buffalo’s
locations.blurb: The latest in a long line of failing restaurants opened in this location. Serves global fusion cuisine.

locations.name: City Medical Center
locations.blurb: An enormous hospital complex housing some of the best medical staff and technology in Night City.

locations.name: The Garden of Earthly Delights
locations.blurb: A full hedonistic experience brothel. A visit starts with dinner and ends with time spent with meat puppets programmed to the client’s specifications.

locations.name: GraffitiX
locations.blurb: An art gallery displaying the work of Night City’s best up-and-coming artists.

locations.name: La Lune Blue
locations.blurb: A high-end French restaurant.

locations.name: Marina FloatHomes
locations.blurb: A collection of small houseboats for rent.

locations.name: McCartney Cubes
locations.blurb: A cube hotel near the stadium.

locations.name: McCartney Field Stadium
locations.blurb: A 75,000 seat stadium and the heart of Night City’s sports and concert scene. Franchises calling the stadium home include the Slammers (Baseball), Heat (Basketball), Death Dealers (Combat Soccer), Nuke (Murderball), and the New Battlegrounds Championship Wrestling League.

locations.name: Night City Bubbles
locations.blurb: A high-end spa. Some employees can be hired as escorts for the evening.

locations.name: REO Meatwagon Offices
locations.blurb: Home of Night City’s second-biggest EMS operation.

locations.name: TravlStay CityCenter
locations.blurb: A cube hotel with paper-thin walls and absolutely no security.

locations.name: Ziggurat Offices
locations.blurb: The headquarters of Ziggurat, the company responsible for building and maintaining Citinets across the continent. Attached is the Hanging Gardens, which provides housing for employees.

districts.name: Downtown
districts.blurb: A new district carved out of Little Europe by Mister Kernighan and a consortium of Fixers and Execs known as the Chamber of Commerce. Downtown is preparing for Night City’s full rebirth by creating the most commercially friendly district on the Island.
districts.cityManager: Emilia Ortega (appointed by Chamber of Commerce)

locations.name: Acadia Way
locations.blurb: A single street containing restored bungalows, gated away from the rest of the world.

locations.name: Continental Brands Offices
locations.blurb: The Night City headquarters of food juggernaut Continental Brands. Also home to the Oasis Megamart, the largest grocery store in the city.

locations.name: Cortex Complex
locations.blurb: An ugly office building that vaguely resembles a human brain. Home to Jack Skorkowski Real Estate and DizCom, an industrial design firm.

locations.name: Delirium
locations.blurb: A gothpunk virtuality club.

locations.name: Night City Firestation #2
locations.blurb: The most wellfunded firestation in Night City. It is well fortified, well equipped, and employs a number of FBC firefighters.

districts.name: The Hot Zone
districts.blurb: Formerly the central city Corporate Zone. Now, a bleak landscape riddles with twisted, wrecked skyscrapers. It shrinks a bit each year as the edges are cleared and rebuilt.

locations.name: The Ashcroft Hotel
locations.blurb: Once the most luxurious hotel in Night City. Now the center of Maelstrom’s Hot Zone scavenging operations.

locations.name: The N54
locations.blurb: The former home of Network 54 in Night City. The tallest structure still standing in the Hot Zone – climbing it and tagging the top has become a tradition among urbanauts.

locations.name: Toggle’s Temple
locations.blurb: An underground firearms range and obstacle course run by a conspiracy theorist named Toggle.

locations.name: Totentanz
locations.blurb: A chrome metal club and home base for Maelstrom. You smell like a cop. Know what we do to cops we catch sniffing around Totentanz ? We feed ‘em to The Pit! — Quake Maelstrom Lieutenant

districts.name: Little China
districts.blurb: A struggling community attempting to crawl its way out of the combat zones and into the rebuilding urban center.
districts.cityManager: David Ling Po (appointed by the Little China Redevelopment Association)

locations.name: Bridgetown
locations.blurb: A cargo container community stacked under the end of the Pelican Boulevard overpass. It isn’t uncommon for bodies to wash up on the waterfront nearby.

locations.name: Chrome Cross
locations.blurb: A dive bar frequented by the Red Chrome Legion.

locations.name: Forlorn Hope
locations.blurb: The home of The Forlorn Hope, a venerable edgerunner bar and Night City institution (before the events of Tales of the RED: Hope Reborn).

locations.name: Guăngbō Tower
locations.blurb: A symbol of Little China’s aspirations for the future, this restored tower houses a number of organizations and businesses, including the Ling Po Public Library and Virtex’s Virtuality Venue.

locations.name: Prosperity Gardens Tenements
locations.blurb: A block of mixed-use apartments holding way too many people. For mysterious reasons, it is also one of the safest places to live in Little China.

districts.name: University District
districts.blurb: A slim district housing the city’s only traditional institution of higher learning.

locations.name: Biotechnica Campus
locations.blurb: The headquarters of Biotechnica in Night City. Strange sounds can be heard from the campus at night.

locations.name: Biotechnica Habitation Sphere Alpha
locations.blurb: A geodesic dome serving as housing for Biotechnica employees.

locations.name: Night City Symphony Hall
locations.blurb: A performance space owned and operated by the Philharmonic Vampyres.

locations.name: Night City University
locations.blurb: A college campus built up into something of a fortified monastery. The center of higher education in Night City.

locations.name: Parkside Living
locations.blurb: Apartments occupied primarily by NCU students and some faculty. Always loud and boisterous.

locations.name: Princessland!
locations.blurb: An abandoned carnival themed around an old animated show. Now home to the Princesses of Justice.

locations.name: Stems & Seeds
locations.blurb: A guerilla gardening operation run by Lily Larson, a former researcher for Petrochem.

locations.name: University Cubes
locations.blurb: Cheap rooms for university students on a budget.

locations.name: Yewtree
locations.blurb: A neo-hipster bar working in collusion with NCU Security to keep students quiet while drinking in the district.

districts.name: The Glen
districts.blurb: The administrative center of Night City; full of movers, shakers, and power players.

locations.name: 1st Night City Bank
locations.blurb: The largest bank in Night City and the most likely source of loan money for local projects (usually lent to people with plenty of money of their own).

locations.name: Air
locations.blurb: An oxygen bar for those who can afford the fresh stuff.

locations.name: Bear’s
locations.blurb: Famous for its microbrew selection and the moth-eaten bear head sitting above the bar.

locations.name: City Hall
locations.blurb: The seat of local government in Night City.

locations.name: City Police Precinct #1
locations.blurb: The first line of defense against the gangs of the combat zones … for those who can afford it.

locations.name: Club Atlantis
locations.blurb: A glamorous, multi-level club with a flashy, avant-garde, and disorienting style.

locations.name: Glenlife Perfected
locations.blurb: An apartment building. Looks great on the outside. Not so great on the inside.

locations.name: Hall of Justice
locations.blurb: Courthouse and jail all in one. An imposing, brutalist structure.

locations.name: Kasim’s
locations.blurb: A Turkish coffee and tobacco bar. Closed on Fridays so the owner and his family can attend prayers.

locations.name: Merrill, Asukaga & Finch Offices
locations.blurb: The Night City headquarters of the world’s largest independent financial and investment institution. The tall skyscraper houses additional businesses.

locations.name: Night City Plaza
locations.blurb: A beautiful park open to the public. The largest green space in Night City.

locations.name: Raven Microcybernetics
locations.blurb: Night City headquarters for a major cybernetics company. The skyscraper also houses some of the company’s close business partners.

locations.name: Seafoam
locations.blurb: A cube hotel close to Club Atlantis. The party never stops here, though revelers sometimes wake up after a bender missing money, inventory, or chrome courtesy of the Reckoners.

districts.name: Old Japantown
districts.blurb: Most of Night City’s ethnic Japanese population has moved north, but enough still cling together here to form islands of civilization in a sea of combat zone chaos.
districts.cityManager: Adriane Casselle (elected by local family heads)

locations.name: Crisis Medical Center
locations.blurb: A no-questions asked medical center supplied with surprisingly advanced technology. Multiple Corps use it as a staging ground to run medical experiments.

locations.name: Highcourt Plaza Hotel
locations.blurb: A classy and well-defended hotel providing excellent service. Most guests arrive via AV to avoid driving through a combat zone.

locations.name: Honest Hiro’s Used Cars
locations.blurb: A used car dealership supplied by the Steel Vaqueros (and other nomads) and protected by edgerunners who trade service for vehicles.

locations.name: Mrs. Suzuki’s Bodega
locations.blurb: The most secure and stable market in Old Japantown. Known for being the only distribution point for mushrooms grown by the Shroomers.

locations.name: The Precipice
locations.blurb: A cargo container community. Many of the residents earn extra cash by volunteering for experiments at Crisis Medical.

locations.name: Unnamed Cube Hotel
locations.blurb: The rooms are cleaned out by ceiling-mounted water jets, and the locks on the doors are dodgy, but at least there are no cameras and no questions.

districts.name: South Night City
districts.blurb: A sprawling mix of industry and residential buildings. It is a combat zone primarily because the city manager, Gaven Haakensen, cares more about lining his pockets than he does doing his job. That doesn’t make him unusual, but he’s more blatant about it than most.

locations.name: The Boneyard
locations.blurb: Formerly the Night City Garden of Rest. Now a shanty town and home to the Sinful Adams. They run an annual festival on Halloween for the district’s residents.

locations.name: MindNutz Lover
locations.blurb: The hottest braindance club in South Night City.

locations.name: Savage Docs
locations.blurb: A multi-ripperdoc operation of good reputation protected by both the Yakuza and the Tyger Claws (despite their differences).

locations.name: Silverhand Studios
locations.blurb: Apartments and studio space rented out to artists and musicians. Run by the cousin of legendary Rockerboy Kerry Eurodyne.

locations.name: The Slammer
locations.blurb: A ganger bar. Home of the Arena, a no-holds-barred combat ring gangers can step into to settle their disputes without murder.

locations.name: South Cargo Village
locations.blurb: A cargo container community. Despite being on the border of The Glen, it is still in a combat zone, and the cops treat it as such.

locations.name: Union Chapel Building
locations.blurb: Once an architectural landmark. Now abandoned, in theory. Some think the Reckoners use the basement as a refuge.

locations.name: University Cargo Bay
locations.blurb: Cargo container housing for university students.

districts.name: Port of Night City
districts.blurb: A central location for cargo entering and leaving Night City by sea. Run by nomads from the Thelas Nation.

locations.name: Dock 13
locations.blurb: The storefront (and occasional night market) of marketing genius Willy “Mister Amaaaze” Maze.

locations.name: Dock 14 Studio Apartments
locations.blurb: An apartment building just one dock away from the always loud Dock 13.

locations.name: Dock Cargo Community
locations.blurb: A cargo container community nestled between the docks.

locations.name: Flotsam
locations.blurb: A small drift town just off the coast. It consists of several larger vessels run aground connected by smaller boats, rafts, and walkways. The Randy Dandy, a mobile bar, often docks here.

locations.name: Medical Technologies
locations.blurb: A body bank specializing in growing replacement limbs. Known for buying and selling dodgy cyberware as well.

locations.name: Rusty’s Dive Shack
locations.blurb: A rough-and-tumble bar for sea-faring types. Built out of the bridge of an old container sub.

locations.name: South Night City Reclaimed Studio
locations.blurb: An apartment building near the water. Leaving the building risks encountering gangers visiting Medical Technologies.

districts.name: Reclamation Zone
districts.blurb: A small enclave run by nomads turned reclaimers. They’ve taken over the operation of Night City’s public transportation, exchanging their technical and motor skills for the land.

locations.name: Herschel’s Crematorium
locations.blurb: A funeral home run by an undertaker who truly believes everyone deserves a dignified sendoff into the next life.

districts.name: Old Combat Zone
districts.blurb: In the late 2010s and early 2020s, Night City began expanding the Island by filling in land to the southeast. In the aftermath of the 4th Corporate War, what was intended to be a shining beacon of industrial might devolved into the worst combat zone Night City had ever seen. Slowly, inch by inch, groups of edgerunners have strived to rebuild it.
districts.cityManager: Brick Coleman (as leader of Edgerunners Inc)

locations.name: From the Ashes
locations.blurb: A sliding scale clinic run by Phoenix Redwyne.

locations.name: Jesse James’ Kosher Deli
locations.blurb: More of a saloon than a deli, though for a small fortune you can get a pretty good corned beef on rye.

locations.name: NC Ionic Semiconductor Building
locations.blurb: A factory-turned-cargo community. Many Iron Sights stash family members here for safety.

locations.name: The Underground
locations.blurb: The home of the Shroomers, located deep beneath the streets of Night City. N orthside n o r t h s i d e n o r t h s i d e The land to the north of the island. Once home to forest and parks, now home to megabuildings, the masses, and the military.

districts.name: NorCal Military Base
districts.blurb: Home of the Estero Bay Military COG (a mixture of various military units into a single organized group). In theory, the COG is loyal to NorCal and the Pacifica Confederation, but they’ve also made a deal with Militech, trading land and access for training and munitions.

locations.name: Militech Corporate Operatives Housing
locations.blurb: Secure housing for Militech employees.

locations.name: Militech Offices
locations.blurb: Night City headquarters for Militech, a one-stop shop for all your military and security needs.

districts.name: Watson Development
districts.blurb: A developing district built up by the Night City Co-Prosperity Sphere (NCCS), an alliance of various Corporations (primarily of Japanese origin). Last year, community organizer Lucius Rhyne led a district-wide labor strike, forcing the NCCS to organize a general election for City Manager. Rhyne won the resulting race handily.

locations.name: City Police Precinct #3
locations.blurb: A large, well-armed police precinct. The egos of some cops here took a bruising when they were unable to break up the labor strike.

locations.name: HTown
locations.blurb: A tent city built outside the walls of a gated community. Tensions are high.

locations.name: Petrochem & SovOil Joint Temporary Housing Solution
locations.blurb: In a twist of irony, both Petrochem and SovOil provide employee housing in the same building. No one is happy about it.

locations.name: Petrochem Offices
locations.blurb: The heavily defended headquarters of Petrochem in Night City. There’s a small museum dedicated to the history of petroleum. Across the street from the SovOil Offices.

locations.name: Red Oktober
locations.blurb: A Soviet-themed bar built into an old subway station.

locations.name: Redline
locations.blurb: Home of the most thrilling bloodsport in Night City and the Wild Things, a gang dedicated to organized competitive violence.

locations.name: Sakura’s
locations.blurb: A Night City interpretation of an izakaya, an informal bar.

locations.name: Smash/Cut
locations.blurb: An EDM club where the chromed up go to dance, do drugs, and have anonymous sex.

locations.name: SovOil Offices
locations.blurb: Night City headquarters for SovOil. Completely off-limits to the public. Across the street from the Petrochem Offices.

locations.name: Trauma Team Corporate Living Center
locations.blurb: Housing for Trauma Team employees.

locations.name: Trauma Team Tower
locations.blurb: Night City headquarters for Trauma Team. Includes an AV repair bay and a hospital for the exclusive use of Executive-level clients.

locations.name: Vargtimmen
locations.blurb: A neo-pagan mead bar. Famous for their solstice and equinox parties.

locations.name: Watson Central Cubelife
locations.blurb: A bog standard cube hotel. Let’s all welcome Manager Lucius Rhyne to the Council. I’m sure we all look forward to working with him. With that out of the way, let ’s begin the vote on Manager Lee’s bill to authorize the use of lethal force when dealing with labor strikes. — From the Night City Council Records

districts.name: Kabuki
districts.blurb: A small district centered around the Nakagawa Kabuki Theater. Common wisdom holds that while Watson acts as the arms and legs of the Night City Co-Prosperity Sphere, Kabuki is its brain and heart.

locations.name: Nakagawa Kabuki Theater
locations.blurb: The most magnificent building in Northside. Home to a Kabuki troupe said to be the equal of any in Japan, as well as a museum and the central offices of the Tyger Claws leadership.

locations.name: Yum Seng
locations.blurb: A host and hostess bar famous for its seafood and soundproof karaoke boxes. M ainland m a i n l a n d m a i n l a n d The overpacked suburbs, struggling to rebuild in the Time of the Red.

districts.name: New Westbrook
districts.blurb: An urban sprawl built in the remains of an upscale suburb. It mixes glitz and glam with tent cities and lowrent housing. Most of the northern part of the district is occupied by a walled-off fake city where Network 54 runs and films The Combat Zone, a battle royale “game show” in which fifty people enter and only one gets to leave alive with a year’s worth of real chicken dinners as the prize.
districts.cityManager: Belkis Abera (appointed by WorldSat and Network 54)

locations.name: Canalside Plaza
locations.blurb: A strip mall. Home to the Sizzle Jams Talent Agency, a Rickshaws, a Capitán Caliente restaurant, the Mane Event hair and nail salon, and an Oasis.

locations.name: Chatelaine’s
locations.blurb: An early 20th-century style cabaret and burlesque queer club so popular it attracts a number of straight tourists.

locations.name: Dilly’s
locations.blurb: A love hotel with a unique mascot – a cartoon pickle wearing a rolled-up condom as a beanie.

locations.name: Evergreen Apartments
locations.blurb: A former big box store transformed into a cube hotel. For the right price, the landlord is more than happy to evict existing tenants for you.

locations.name: Network 54 Offices
locations.blurb: The Night City headquarters and broadcasting tower for Network 54.

locations.name: Network 54 Westbrook Private Acres
locations.blurb: A gated community of duplexes for the use of Network 54 employees.

locations.name: Night City Firestation #1
locations.blurb: A well-supplied firestation. It specializes in AV-based firefighting.

locations.name: North Cargo Village
locations.blurb: A cargo container community stacked in an abandoned parking lot.

locations.name: Rocklin Augmentics Campus
locations.blurb: Night City headquarters of Rocklin Augmentics, including offices, meeting spaces, and a research hospital.

locations.name: Rocklin Augmentics Innovation Hub
locations.blurb: Corporate housing for Rocklin Augmentics employees. They are encouraged to use the various maker spaces built inside.

locations.name: WorldSat Offices
locations.blurb: A heavily defended compound on the edge of the city. It is not only the local headquarters of WorldSat but also the junction point for satellite communications between Night City and the outside world.

districts.name: Charter Hill
districts.blurb: A small but influential community. On a clear day, the residents of Charter Hill can see the walls of the Exec Zone and dream of climbing even higher on the Corporate ladder.

locations.name: Anjelika’s
locations.blurb: A host and hostess bar catering to clients with a heavy cyberware fetish.

locations.name: Bella Mia
locations.blurb: A club where the affluent and most fashionable residents of Night City go to be seen.

locations.name: L’Ermitage
locations.blurb: A high-end apartment complex. Most of the units are rented on a short-term basis by Execs visiting Night City for a prolonged period of time.

locations.name: Seral Grove
locations.blurb: An art installation turned high-end burial ground located beneath the district. Burial packages include digital reconstructions of the deceased so visitors can “speak” to their loved ones.

districts.name: Exec Zone
districts.blurb: The single most secure district in Night City. Only the truly elite live here.
districts.cityManager: Doctor Karen Davies (elected by Home Owner’s Association)

districts.name: Heywood Docks
districts.blurb: As the world returns to normal, Corporations are looking to cut the nomad nations out of the shipping and logistics equation. Larger vessels can’t use the Heywood Docks, but smaller, Corporate-sponsored ships moving up and down the West Coast can.

locations.name: Greenbox Storage Units
locations.blurb: Technically a secure storage facility, but customers have been known to live inside the units.

districts.name: North Heywood
districts.blurb: Over the past decade, Heywood has been divided into two districts. In the north are workaday residents, many of whom have found jobs in the nearby Heywood Industrial Zone.
districts.cityManager: Barry “Big Deal” Delvecchio (appointed by district council)

locations.name: Acorn Towers
locations.blurb: A dual-tower apartment complex housing Dynalar employees.

locations.name: The Armory
locations.blurb: A former National Guard armory transformed into the headquarters of 6th Street.

locations.name: Biotechnica Palm Grove
locations.blurb: A grove of experimental palm trees owned and monitored by Biotechnica.

locations.name: Converted Motel Studio Apartments
locations.blurb: A no-name motel transformed into no-name apartments on the edge of the city.

locations.name: Dynalar Campus
locations.blurb: The regional headquarters of Dynalar, a popular cyberware and electronics company.

locations.name: Forlorn Hope
locations.blurb: The home of The Forlorn Hope, a venerable edgerunner bar and Night City institution (after the events of Tales of the RED: Hope Reborn).

locations.name: Nana Meow’s Nursery
locations.blurb: Not a guerilla garden itself but a shop that supplies gear and seeds to guerilla gardeners.

locations.name: Night City Animal Shelter
locations.blurb: A former veterinarian clinic now occupied by a ripperdoc. It specializes in Exotics and Bioexotics.

locations.name: Woodland Park
locations.blurb: A small neighborhood near the Dynalar campus. Highlights include the Burning Bright Bodega, Breeze (a mom and pop drug store), the Palms cargo container community, the Shark apartment building, and the Zolletta cube hotel.

locations.name: Xanadu
locations.blurb: A roller derby rink and disco tech. Home of the Muses.

districts.name: Heywood Industrial Zone
districts.blurb: The largest industrial zone in Night City, overflowing with warehouses, construction equipment, factories, and even some derelict cargo ships.
districts.cityManager: Theo Walker (appointed by the Arroyo Concern)

locations.name: D.V. Rambling Rose
locations.blurb: An ancient vessel stuck in dry dock. Home base for Fixie’s Couriers.

locations.name: Old Ironworks Building
locations.blurb: The inside has been converted into apartments, and the landlords have stacked cargo container housing on the roof.

locations.name: Yang’s Wheels
locations.blurb: The headquarters, manufacturing factory, and warehouse of Yang’s Wheels, Night City’s biggest provider of inexpensive wheeled transportation.

locations.name: Zhirafa Office Park
locations.blurb: The Night City headquarters of Zhirafa. Drones are used for both labor and S security.

locations.name: Zhirafa Office Park MicroVillage
locations.blurb: Corporate housing for Zhirafa employees, colorfully disguised as cargo containers.

districts.name: Santo Domingo
districts.blurb: South Heywood is better known by the locals as Santo Domino. The nomad camp near the dam heavily influences the district, but the Aldecaldos power may be waning. Theresa Valentino, an independent candidate, recently won the election for City Manager thanks to backing from the El Norte cartel.

locations.name: Aldecaldo Camp
locations.blurb: A large multi-cultural encampment sitting at the base of the Petrochem dam. While all nomads are welcome, the camp is primarily dominated by the Aldecaldos.

locations.name: City Police Precinct #2
locations.blurb: Large but overworked, the cops here rely heavily on drones to patrol their beats.

locations.name: East Cargo Village
locations.blurb: A dusty cargo container community located near the edge of the city.

locations.name: Heywood Suites
locations.blurb: An apartment complex situated beneath one of the most heavily trafficked overpasses in Night City. Many residents have level-dampening cyberware installed.

locations.name: María’s
locations.blurb: A family-owned beer tent located just inside the city limits.

locations.name: MetalStorm
locations.blurb: A seemingly indestructible bar located under the Pacifica Bridge. Popular with FBCs.

locations.name: Woodchipper’s Garage
locations.blurb: The home base of Woodchipper, the most influential nomad Fixer in Night City. She throws her famous Night Markets/ block parties in the cul-de-sac to the southwest. S outhside s o u t h s i d e s o u t h s i d e One part vacation spot, one part urban wasteland.

districts.name: Pacifica Playground
districts.blurb: A district built around Playland by the Sea.
districts.cityManager: Elliot Kane (appointed by Playland by the Sea management)

locations.name: Bits’n’Bolts
locations.blurb: A hole-in-the-wall tech shop with connections to weaponsmith and inventor Faisal.

locations.name: Cubeland by the Sea
locations.blurb: A shoddy cube hotel a stone’s throw away from Playland by the Sea.

locations.name: Mister Rice Guy
locations.blurb: An upscale sushi restaurant. Famous for its mascot, Hime Cat.

locations.name: Playhouse
locations.blurb: An apartment complex with a shady past. Rumors suggest it is haunted.

locations.name: Playland by the Sea
locations.blurb: Night City’s premiere tourist destination. An amusement park sponsored by various Corporations. The Piranahs hold sway here, and it is home to a surprising number of yogangs (often used by the park as free labor).

locations.name: Pleasant Valley Apartments
locations.blurb: An apartment building designed for neo-luddites who want to escape from technoshock overload.

locations.name: Scenic Cubes
locations.blurb: A cube hotel covered in some of the most expressive graffiti in Night City.

locations.name: The XX (The Twenty)
locations.blurb: A dive punk bar. Breakfist, the owner, serves juice instead of booze.

districts.name: Rancho Coronado
districts.blurb: Technically part of Night City, no one has yet bothered to pony up the cash to buy Rancho Coronado’s seat on the City Council. As a result, the district lacks in just about every resource, from utilities to fire and police services.

locations.name: Albino Alligator Carwash
locations.blurb: Home base for the Albino Alligators. Also one of the most reliable places to find clean drinking water in the district.

locations.name: Coronado Heights
locations.blurb: An apartment building so close to Pacifica that it might as well be part of it.

locations.name: Eagle Rock Stadium
locations.blurb: A former football field transformed into a cargo container community.

locations.name: Jack ‘N’ the Green
locations.blurb: A guerilla gardening outfit run by reclaimers.

locations.name: Minimallism
locations.blurb: Once a mall catering to eager beaverville consumers, now an empty husk claimed on one side by reclaimers and on the other by a consortium of Fixers who take turns running Night Markets there. Also known as the RC Night Market by residents. N ight City Gangs n i g h t c i t y g a n A brief guide to Night City’s gangs and criminal orgag s nizations. This list is likely incomplete since old gangs die and new gangs rise up all the time. 6th Street: Formed by veterans of the 4th Corporate War, 6th Street tries to earn money through security contracts but has been forced to move into extortion and smuggling to pay the bills. Albino Alligators: A party gang with a surprisingly significant influence on Rancho Coronado. Famous for their white alligator cartoon mascot and popped shirt collars. The Andersons: An aging yogang with a family theme. In danger of being swallowed up by the Piranhas. Arzin Tynon: An older boostergang operating on the northern edges of Night City. The Bozos: A prankster gang (for a certain deadly definition of prankster) with a clown theme. Currently engaged in a civil war of pranks and mayhem. Consortium: A tightly organized Russian mob group with ties to the Thelas nomad nation. Culper Ring: A secret sect within the Estero Bay Military COG dedicated to reuniting NorCal with the US. DeadWoods: A cowboy-themed gang. They act as self-appointed protectors of Night City’s railways. The Dirty Hippies: A group of guerilla gardeners who specialize in the growing and sale of herbs laced with various drugs, collectively known as ganga. Dragula Racers: A monster-themed racing gogang. Eastern Tigers Triad: An organized crime ring recently arrived from China. Edgerunners Inc: A group of younger edgerunners seeking to reconnect the Old Combat Zone to Night City. Named after a pre-war company. El Norte Cartel: A Mexican criminal organization establishing itself in Night City. Said to be connected to Theresa Valentino, the Santo Domingo City Manager. The Enhanced: A cult that believes cyberpsychosis represents the next stage of human evolution. Eurotrashers: A party gang in Little Europe. All members speak with a “European” accent no one can identify. The Faded: A group of older edgerunners who want to keep Night City from interfering with the Old Combat Zone. Fixie’s Couriers: A collective of bicycle messengers and couriers guided (not led) by a Fixer known as Fixie. G3: A disturbingly violent anime-themed poser gang. Generation Red: A yogang operating out of the Old Combat Zone. Gold Dragons: A gang under the control of David Ling Po, providing protection in Little China. Inquisitors: A cult centered on the belief that cyberware is evil and ripping it out of others saves their souls. Iron Sights: A brutal combat gang. Their new sponsor, a Fixer named Hornet, has built them into a force to be reckoned with. Kanzaki Family: The only surviving faction of Yakuza left in Night City. At odds with the Tyger Claws. Kill Krashers: A relatively new gang glorifying violence above all else. Growing with surprising speed. Lightning Cats: A Bioexotic cat gang operating out of the Hot Zone. Maelstrom: A combat gang with a might makes right philosophy. Their leader, Warlock, has transformed Maelstom into a surprisingly effective criminal enterprise. Mudang Gumi: A gang of Netrunners and burglars focused on data theft. The Muses: A poser gang and roller derby squad with a fusion disco/Greek mythology theme. Philharmonic Vampyres: A gang with a split personality, trying to decide if it should lean into its artistic goth side or stick to its prankster roots. Piranhas: Night City’s premiere party gang. These days they don’t just attend the best parties. They throw them. Princesses of Justice: A poser gang based on an old animated show. Offers protection to those victims of abuse. Rat Kings: A small boostergang operating out of the still-under-construction H4 Megabuilding. Reckoners: A nihilistic cult preaching about an upcoming Harvest of Souls. Always looking for donations, often from someone’s unconscious body. Red Chrome Legion: A neo-nazi hate group locked in a war of attrition with the Iron Sights. Scavvers: Not a single gang but a group of them, all surviving by scavenging tech from ruins and combat zones. The Sinful Adams: A goth poser gang living in the South Night City boneyard. Skiv Family: Night City’s dominant mafia family. They control the Heywood Docks. Steel Vaqueros: A nomad pack operating up and down the west coast. They recruit locals to act as junior members of the pack and “hold down the fort” while they are on the road. The Prime-Time Players: A poser gang, usually inspired by old sitcoms and television shows. Broken up into a number of different factions based on theme. The Shroomers: Part survivalist group, part guerilla gardener collective. The Shroomers live beneath the streets of the Old Combat Zone, where they grow various fungi. The Street Queens: A guardian gang dedicated to protecting the queer residents and neighborhoods of Night City. The Toecutters: A Raffen Shiv clan operating on the eastern edges of Night City. Said by some to be cannibals. Tombstone Preservers: A guardian gang dedicated to protecting the sanctity of the dead. Tyger Claws: A former Araska proxy gang, the Tyger Claws are now a dominant force in Kabuki and Old Japantown where they control both security and the criminal element. Undertow: A gang operating in Little Europe and Downtown. They claim to be fighting against gentrification, but their violence often harms the very neighborhoods they’re trying to protect. Voodoo Boys: Posers who drape themselves in Hollywood-style “voodoo” trappings. Violent and focused primarily on the drug trade. Weng Fang Tong: A major crime syndicate with fingers in gambling and sex work across Night City. Run by David Ling Po. Wild Things: A boostergang that channels its violent impulses through gladiatorial combat at the Redline. Willows: Less a gang and more a therapy group made up of female combat veterans. Yellow Brick Road Gang: A poser gang modeled after The Wizard of Oz. The Zoners: A movement dedicated to improving the living conditions in South Night City through community organization and protest.

map.note: Marker coordinates are percentages of the stitched Night City Atlas map (pages 4-5).

travel.note: Travel times are a Night City Tales house rule, not a Cyberpunk RED printed value. They are no longer a flat table: the engine routes across the district graph in night-city-map.json and prices the distance at the speed of whatever the character is travelling by.

scale.note: House rule. The atlas prints no scale bar, so this comes off the map's own street grid: a city block in the University District measures about 1.33% of the map's width, which at a 120m block puts 1% at roughly 90m. That makes the drawn city about 7km across and 9km top to bottom.

travel.withinDistrictNote: Crossing part of one district without leaving it. Half a district's width is the house-rule distance for an errand close to home.
travel.defaultStartNote: House rule: a character with no recorded address starts in Little Europe, the atlas's dense mixed-income residential district. The atlas does not assign starting addresses.
